title: File system (fs)
lede: Node-fs-shaped file I/O for config, data, and logs. The sync set is the core; async variants (callback + Promise) and read/write streams wrap the same runtime helpers. The recurring divergence is text-first: the plain readFileSync/readFile/stream path is strlen-based and truncates at an embedded null byte — use readFileSyncBytes / an ArrayBuffer write for binary. There is no Buffer class (plain ArrayBuffer/TypedArrays), and the async variants are an API shape, not a concurrency gain (blocking I/O under the hood).

entries.name: fs.readFileSync(path)
entries.description: Reads the whole file into a string. Throws a catchable Error (built from strerror(errno)) if the file can't be opened.
differences: Text-only by design — a file with embedded null bytes reads back shorter than its real size (`.length` is `strlen`-based); use `fs.readFileSyncBytes(path)` for a binary file.

entries.name: fs.readFileSyncBytes(path)
entries.description: Binary-safe sibling of readFileSync: returns a Uint8Array with the file's exact byte count (no strlen involved), so a file with an embedded null byte reads back whole. There is no Buffer class — this compiler uses plain ArrayBuffer/TypedArrays.

entries.name: fs.writeFileSync(path, data)
entries.signature: writeFileSync(path: string, data: string | ArrayBuffer | TypedArray): void
entries.description: Creates or truncates the file with data, throwing on failure. data may be a string (the strlen-based path) or an ArrayBuffer/TypedArray (binary-safe, writes the real byte count via fwrite) — dispatched on data's inferred type.

params.name: data
params.desc: Content; binary for the typed-array forms.

entries.name: fs.appendFileSync(path, data)
entries.signature: appendFileSync(path: string, data: string | ArrayBuffer | TypedArray): void
entries.description: Like writeFileSync, but appends instead of truncating (creates the file if it doesn't exist). Throws on failure. Same string/ArrayBuffer/TypedArray dispatch as writeFileSync.

entries.name: fs.existsSync(path)
entries.description: Plain existence check via POSIX access(). Deliberately does not throw for a missing path — matching real Node's own existsSync, one of the few fs functions that reports "doesn't exist" as false rather than an error.

entries.name: fs.unlinkSync(path)
entries.description: Deletes a file. Throws on failure.

entries.name: fs.mkdirSync(path)
entries.description: Creates a directory via POSIX mkdir(), mode 0777 reduced by the process umask as usual.
differences: No `{recursive: true}` option — throws (e.g. `EEXIST`) if the path already exists or a parent directory is missing.

entries.name: fs.rmdirSync(path)
entries.description: Removes an empty directory via POSIX rmdir() — deliberately directory-only (fails on a plain file, unlike unlinkSync).
differences: No recursive-delete option, matching `mkdirSync`'s lack of one.

entries.name: fs.readdirSync(path)
entries.description: Lists a directory's entries (excluding . and ..) as a string[], in whatever order the OS's own readdir() returns them — no ordering guarantee, matching real Node. Verified on both Darwin and x86-64 Linux via a compiled offsetof probe.

entries.name: fs.renameSync(oldPath, newPath)
entries.description: Renames/moves a file via POSIX rename(). Throws on failure.

entries.name: fs.copyFileSync(src, dest)
entries.description: Copies a file by composing the raw byte-count-aware read/write helpers — binary-safe, so a source file with an embedded null byte copies back whole. No new C-level I/O code.

entries.name: Async variants (callback + fs.promises)
entries.statusRow: Async variants — callback (`fs.readFile(path, cb)`) + Promise (`fs.promises.readFile` / `import from 'fs/promises'`)
entries.description: Async forms of the sync set: readFile/writeFile/appendFile/unlink/mkdir/rmdir/rename/copyFile/readdir. The callback gets (err[, data]); the Promise rejects with the same Error the sync form throws. Each reuses its *Sync runtime helper verbatim, catching the throw via the compiler's setjmp catch primitive — no parallel non-throwing I/O code.
entries.snippet:
await fs.promises.writeFile('demo.txt', 'hi')
const text: string = await fs.promises.readFile('demo.txt')
differences: Blocking I/O under the hood — no thread pool, so the syscall runs inline; only *delivery* is async (the callback fires right after the op, the Promise is returned already settled). An API-shape gain, not a concurrency/performance one.
`readFile` delivers a string (text) — inherits `readFileSync`'s text-only caveat; no async binary (`Buffer`) form.
No `options`/`encoding` argument; no async `stat` (no sync `stat` exists either).

entries.name: fs.createReadStream / createWriteStream
entries.signature: fs.createReadStream(path, opts?): Readable; fs.createWriteStream(path, opts?): Writable
entries.description: createReadStream returns a Node Readable (consume via for await, .on('data')/.on('end'), or .pipe()); createWriteStream a Node Writable (.write/.end, 'finish'/'close'/'drain'). A read→write .pipe() round-trips; a failed open throws a catchable Error.
differences: Chunks are **strings**, not `Buffer`s — text-first, like `readFileSync` (an embedded NUL truncates a chunk); binary (`Uint8Array`) streaming is a follow-on.
`createReadStream` reads eagerly to EOF at construction (chunked, not a lazy pull) — a huge file is fully read into per-chunk buffers.
Options: `createReadStream` takes `{ highWaterMark }`, `createWriteStream` `{ flags: "w"|"a" }` — both compile-time literals; `start`/`end`/`fd`/`encoding` are clean errors.

entries.name: fs.statSync(path) / fs.lstatSync(path)
entries.description: Reads file metadata into a Stats object. lstatSync does not follow a final symlink. The Stats value carries size and modified-time plus the type predicates.

returns.desc: A Stats with size, mtimeMs, and isFile()/isDirectory()/isSymbolicLink().

differences: Only `size`, `mtimeMs`, and `isFile()`/`isDirectory()`/`isSymbolicLink()` are exposed — `mode`/`uid`/`atimeMs` and the rest of the Node Stats surface are not.
The Linux struct-stat field offsets are encoded but verified on macOS only so far.

entries.name: fs.rmSync / realpathSync / mkdtempSync / symlinkSync / readlinkSync / chmodSync / truncateSync / accessSync
entries.statusRow: fs.rmSync / realpathSync / mkdtempSync / symlinkSync / readlinkSync / chmodSync / truncateSync / accessSync
entries.signature: rmSync(path: string, options?: { recursive: boolean, force: boolean }): void
entries.description: The rest of the sync path-management set: recursive removal, canonicalization, temp-directory creation, symlink create/read, permission bits, truncation, and existence/permission checks.
differences: `rmSync` options must be a `{ recursive, force }` boolean-literal object — no `maxRetries`/`retryDelay`.
`readlinkSync` caps targets at 4096 bytes; `accessSync`'s mode defaults to existence-only (`F_OK`) with no `fs.constants` to name the others.

entries.name: fs.openSync / closeSync / readSync / writeSync / fstatSync
entries.description: The low-level file-descriptor API: open a path to an fd, read/write at the descriptor, stat it, and close it — for random-access or streaming patterns the whole-file helpers don't cover.

params.name: flags
params.desc: A string-literal mode: r r+ w w+ a a+ wx ax (or a raw numeric mask).

differences: `openSync` flags must be a string literal (`r r+ w w+ a a+ wx ax`) or a raw numeric mask — no `fs.constants` names.
`writeSync` writes string data only (no Buffer/offset/length variant); `readSync`'s buffer must be a `Uint8Array`/`Buffer`.

entries.name: File / FileReader / FileSystemFileHandle
entries.description: The browser-flavored File API is not planned — these model browser sandbox/permission concepts this compiler has no equivalent for. A native CLI/microservice program has direct filesystem access via the fs functions above instead.
